newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma picks ally to head media ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma picks ally to head media ministry.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has appointed a loyal ally to head a new information ministry, his press office said on Thursday.
Kuchma signed a decree late on Wednesday naming Zynoviy Kulyk, widely viewed as very close to the president, as Information Minister.
Kyluk, 49, was the head of the State Television and Radio Committee, which along with the State Information Agency of Ukraine will now be subordinate to his ministry.
Political analysts in Kiev say the changes in Ukraine's information hierarchy show Kuchma is trying to boost his chances of re-election in 1999 by tightening control over the media.
"This clearly shows that Kuchma has already started his campaign," said Mykola Tomenko.
Kuchma said in September that he would run for a second term, warning any potential rivals: "It would not be good for sons to divide the land while the father is still alive."

Kuchma's decree also named Valeriy Mazhynsky as acting head of Kulyk's media committee. Kulyk's appointment signified the end of the old Press and Information Ministry, headed by Mykhailo Onufriychuk.
